rows.name: Laszlo Juhasz
rows.body:
László started climbing in Hungary when he was 16 years old and his enthusiasm and passion for climbing has kept on rising. He has experienced all aspects of climbing; from the mountains of the Alps through to the big vertical cliffs of Yosemite.

Due to László’s travels he has previously experienced a range of climbing styles. Yet now he is choosing to focus more and more on traditional and big wall climbing. For him this is the purest form of climbing.

In addition he has been instructing and coaching for over ten years.

“I have a different grading system for climbing. I prefer to grade it as I enjoy it. For me this is more important.”

rows.name: Pablo Ruiz Seco
rows.body:
Vive en: Reinosa, (Cantabria) una pequeña región en el norte de España

Expariencia escalando: Llevo escalando desde los 14 años y practico todo tipo de escalada. Escalada alpina, clásica, escalada en hielo, bulder, pero sobretodo escalada deportiva.

He escalado en muchos paises de Europa como Italia, Austria Francia, Reino Unido, Eslovenia. Tengo experiencia con haciendo alta montaña en los Alpes en montañas como Cervino, Aiguille Verte, Aiguille de Argentiere y he escalado en en numerosas ocasiones vias de varios largos en hielo en los Alpes.
Tambien practico habitualmente escalada en pared de varios largos en estilo clasico autoprotegiendome en sitios como Dolomitas, Picos de Europa... con rutas como la Comici en la Cima Grande de Lavaredo o varias en la cara oeste del Naranjo de Bulnes en Picos de Europa.

El bulder es algo más esporadico aunque también disfruto y lo que más practico es la escalada de dificultad. Conozco gran cantidad de escuelas en España y paises limítrofes y los últimos dos veranos los paso en Rodellar, (paraíso fanático).

También practico el esquí alpino y esquí de travesía y a lo largo del año hago BTT de vez en cuando.

rows.name: Ritch Mayfield
rows.body:
Rich was born in North Wales in the late 60’s and spent much of his youth climbing and walking in the Welsh hills.  Relocating to Spain more than 10 years ago, was the ‘best move I ever made’ he says.

Rich joined the services shortly after leaving school in 1986, and lived in West Germany for six years, before passing the All Arms Commando Course and moving to Plymouth to serve with 3 Commando. He attended as an incremental member of staff The Army Mountain Training Centre in the Harz Mountains of West Germany, and was an instructor on many expeditions and adventurous training programs.

In 1994 he was invited to participant in the infamous British Army Expedition to Borneo, to descend the North side of Mt Kinabalu via an area known as “Low’s Gully”. The expedition was a spectacular debacle, no communications, poor weather, inappropriate planning, training and equipment, lead to the disintegration of the expedition. Rich was one of the few to have facilitated his own escape, but only after an eight day period with no food. His escape initiated the largest ever peacetime mountain rescue operation which involved over one thousand British and Malayan military personnel in a race against time to find the remaining members of the expedition.

The aftermath of this expedition was acrimonious and Rich received a formal commendation for bravery. So, with a successful book under this belt and a new life in Spain Rich is able to concentrate on his climbing and enjoys his days in the sun guiding for The Orange House.  He has been working professionally as a climbing instructor since 1987 and his personal climbing experience is vast which takes in his early beginnings in Wales, then to Germany and the South West of England.

Rich enjoys all types of climbing and is equally happy on large Trad routes or short Sport routes, from the sea cliffs of Gogarth or The Old Man of Hoy to the steep overhanging crags like “The Wildside” in Sella. Rich is MIA qualified which backs up his former Army experience.

rows.name: Petra Pivoňkova
rows.body: Petra has always loved mountains. She started skiing when she was a little child but didn't get to climbing until she was 25. The later she stared the more she fell in love with it. She redid he life, changed the Czech republic for Spain and started climbing full-time. 'To me climbing is not a sport, it is much more! It is living in the nature, van life, beautiful places and a lot of great friends. Such a life just makes you happy.' In winter she works as a ski teacher in Sierra Nevada but most of the year she lives in Rodellar where she works and climbs. She speaks fluent English and Spanish.

rows.name: Maribel Vara
rows.body:
I tried rock climbing for the first time 12 years ago. I remember that day as putting into practice something that I already knew. It was at a granite slab in La Pedriza, Madrid, my hometown. Since that moment I continued friction climbing for a while, then exploring the rest of the climbable rocks all over the world.

My craving for languages led me to live in different places and of course taste different crags in the US, Italy, Germany, France… After working as a researcher on Ecology and Spanish teacher (among other things), I am currently pursuing my strongest passion and becoming a rock climbing guide.

I very much like sport climbing although lately I am rather psyched to place some gear and jump into beautiful cracks!

rows.name: Daila Ojeda / pro-climber
rows.body: Daila Ojeda started climbing at the age of 18, inspired by a climbing competition in her hometown. Before falling in love with climbing, Daila surfed for many years, something very common in the Canary Islands, her home. After a fes years of climbing, Daila decided to leave the island, and she moved to Catalonia, Spain, one of the best places in the world for rock climbing. For Daila, it was really inspiring to be able to climb with a lot of talented climbers who taught her a lot about the sport and the lifestyle. Since then, Daila has been very active in the community, sending some hard sport routes up to 8c+ (5.14c) and traveling around the world to share her climbing passion. As a female sport climber, she is a role model and has been featured o the covers of climbing magazines around the world. Daila feel very lucky to have climbing in her life.

rows.name: Bérengère Rapeneau
rows.body:
In 2005, she graduates in Sport and Physical Education from the University of Montpellier  with a specialty of adapted sports. She is a certified Climbing Instructor and Canyoning Guide (BEES), which is the only official French certification program designed for canyoning guides. In 2004/2005 she registers as a freelance guide in the French Syndicate of climbing and canyoning professional guides (SNAPEC).

Since 1998, when I started to climb, I have climbed in France, Spain, Morocco, Portugal, Brazil, Argentina…Nowadays I live in Millau in Gorges du Tarn. Thanks to my university studies, which enabled me to work in the field of adapted sports, I have a wide experience working with people with special needs. I also collaborated with many French and Spanish canyoning companies such as Terre d’aventure in Balaquère, Compañía de Guara in Sierra de Guara, Sarrat Sport in Monte Perdido,  Antipodes y Roc et canyon en Ardèche in the Millau region.

rows.name: Will Sim
rows.body:
Will Sim is one of the UK’s leading alpinists and mountaineers. He has climbed big mountains, including first ascents and significant repeats in the Alps, Alaska, Patagonia, Pakistan and the Canadian Rockies.

Will is passionate about every discipline of climbing from high altitude summits to sport climbing. He’s highly experienced in 8b, hard trad, alpine conditions and big walls.

As an IFMGA/UIAGM mountain guide Will holds the highest level of mountain qualification in the world. And, above all, loves to share his passion with others.

rows.name: Klemen Becan
rows.body:
Birthdate: 14.8.1982

Residence: Rakek, Slovenia

Years Climbing: 25

Facebook Page: https://www.facebook.com/kbecan

Instagram: kbecan25

Blog: http://kbecan.blogspot.com/

Video: https://vimeo.com/110348247

Age 7 Klemen tried to climb for the first time and since then all he wanted to do was to climb. Soon he joined the competition group and started to train more seriously and with age 14 he started with international competitions in Slovenian Youth climbing team. He had many good results and age 15 he became world youth champion. In the big competitions it was a little harder and he had to fight from the back of the rankings and in year 2008 he finally got to the top of the podium on World cup competition in Kranj, Slovenia. In bouldering World cups he got two second places in year 2009.

More important for him than competitions was always rock climbing and he spends as much time as possible in the nature. On sight is his favorite thing and in 2004 he did his 1st 8b+ on sight. Many other hard routes followed with the hardest one Siempre se Puede Hacer Menos (https://vimeo.com/117570995) where he did on sight first ascent graded first 8c+ and later downgraded to “only” 8c after finding easier way out at the top. Klemen doesn’t like to spend much time working the routes but he still managed to do some 9a’s from which his favorite is Waterworld in his home carag in Osp (Slovenia) (http://kbecan.blogspot.com/2014/03/big-project-osp.html), where he had to approach with the kayak or later on Tyrolean traverse. In 2016 he climbed his hardest routes graded 9a+ in Oliana (Spain) and also started trying something even harder. At the moment he’s putting a lot of energy into climbing all over Catalonia and sending not just the hardest routes but also enjoying climbing in easier lines which fills him with lots of good energy. Besides climbing Klemen likes to fly. For him successfully topping out the route has never been the main goal. More important is to enjoy the climb, give a big fight and take long fall at the end.

rows.name: Michelle O' Loughlin
rows.body: Michelle began climbing ten years ago and has climbed hard trad up to E7 in her home country of Ireland. Currently she is studying a PhD in psychology. She possesses extensive experience in multipitch-trad thanks to having Fair Head as her home crag, and has put up first ascents in remote parts of Ireland. She has also travelled to places such as Yosemite Valley, and America’s Deep South in search of classic multipitch lines. This spring sees her relocating to Spain to push her sport grade and travel in her van. She helps coach the Irish youth teams and aims to complete her MIA qualification this year. Her other passions include skiing, photography and playing the fiddle!

rows.name: Benjamin Brochard
rows.body:
Benjamin Brochard climbed the library climbing book of his grand father when he was 5 years old. It was his first summit before starting to read them...

"I climbed a lot in the Alpes, where I was born. I love both : sport climbing and multi pitch climbing and throught this sport I 've had the opportunity to travel to many beautiful places like Italy,Spain, Argentina, Jordania, Grecia, Marueco...

When I am not climbing I am practicing ski, ice climbing and alpinism."

I graduated my rock climbing and canyoning teacher licence at 23 and few years later my mountain guide licence.

Between that I graduated my ski patrolman. That 3 officials certifications are certified by ENSA, the National school of ski and alpinism and IFGMA, International Federation of mountain guide association.

Actually, I live my passion and work all around the world in freelance with people between 5 and 100 years old !

Languages : French/Spanish/English

rows.name: Maja Jonjic
rows.body:
My name is Maja Jonjic. I'm 25 years old. I started climbing when I was 15, in my native island, Gran Canaria, and thanks to what the To'patrás club taught me in my beginnings, climbing became my passion.
I trained at the University of Physical Activity and Sports Sciences, but I did not settle for it and I wanted to make my work my way of life. To this day I am also a climbing guide. I combine it working in a climbing wall in the Canary Islands.

About me:

My name is Marta Palou. I fell in love with climbing when I was twelve years old. I started climbing in a gym and competed in national and international competitions for six years. For the past four years, I have been focusing on climbing outside. Since I started climbing I have always been inspired by training. This is why I studied Sports Science. When I finished my degree I moved to Rodellar, where I have climbed routes up to 8c. I spend six months in Rodellar and the other half of the year I live in my van and travel to climb. I have been a qualified trainer and climber for more than thirteen years and have applied my knowledge and experience to personalized training and adapted this to the needs of each person I work with. Climbing is my passion and I love helping others train to reach their own goals in rock climbing.

rows.name: Roberto Munoz Gonzales
rows.body:
Years Climbing: 25

Roberto is our coach and guide for:

  • Big Wall Climbing in Chamonix
  • Multipitch Climbing Course
  • Trad Climbing Course
  • Trad and Multipitch Climbing Private Guide

 

Roberto is one of the Rockbusters and Snowbusters UIAGM mountain guides specializing in Ski Touring, Freeride, and Big Wall Climbing courses. Originally he comes from Madrid, but the call of the big mountains sucked him into Chamonix where he lives since 2014.

He did the UIAGM mountain course at the ENSA also in Chamonix, the oldest guide school in the world.

Now he practices all the sports that the mountains can provide. Skiing in winter and alpinism or rock climbing in summer. He knows very well all the summits around Chamonix where he has climbed some hard routes such as American Direct on the west face of the Drus or Walker Spur on the north face of Grandes Jorasses even he loves guiding his clients into new places both for the clients and him so all the team gets an adventurous experience.

Sport Climbing Performance and Mental Coaching, Deep Water Solo Course, Sport Climbing Road Trips, Multipitch Climbing Course

About Miha:

I will try my best to identify what works best for your further progression or leapfrogging your limitations. Starting from the very basics, or what one might lack, and working on the perception of our motivation for climbing and pushing ourselves.
 
Master’s Degree in Computer Science and Management, working in the field of Research Writing on Science and Technology Literature.

Started climbing quite late, but progressed rapidly to an Onsight level of 7c in just three years. It drastically changed my life to a point of leaving my full-time work and pursuing the need to climb and travel.

I became Climbing Instructor and coach, first licensed in Slovenia, and later continued with SPI AMGA or North American Certification for Single Pitch Instructor for the guiding work in the Caribbean. Continued my profession in Southeast Asia as Private Guide and Deep Water Solo Guide.

Prior to my Climbing career, I trained in Tennis for more than 12 years, and did some competitive Cross-country skiing, and Surfing as a hobby.

I have been attracted by sports and science since I remember, and will try to use both in your climbing development.

rows.name: Matej Hodousek
rows.body:
Birthdate: 06.11.1987

 

Residence: Prague, Czech Republic

 

Years Climbing: 17

 

Facebook Page: https://www.facebook.com/TrenerMatejHodousek

Instagram: @chcipohyb

 

Matej is a fitness specialist and movement therapist focused on climbers.

 

Specialization: 

 

  • Analyzation and correction of climbing movement patterns
  • Injury prevention
  • Rehabilitation after an injury
  • Posture correction
  • Strength and mobility preparation
  • Movement principles for sustainable (long life) climbing
  • Manual technics for pain relief 
  • Basic climbing techniques - proper footwork, correct balance
  • Climbing safety - belay/lead belay, anchor set up, lead climbing, spotting, ... 

 

About Matej:

 

A few years after the university I realized that wood engineering is not my destiny. I started to educate myself in fitness. I began as a coach and climbing instructor. After some years I got a job in a place with a climbing specialization. I worked with many climbers every day. They came to me with finger pain, shoulder, elbow pain, etc. Also, I worked with competitors (the Czech climbing team). I helped them make their movements more efficient and free of any danger to their muscles and tendons. It was complete work containing after-season regeneration and pre-season conditioning of an athlete. I participated in some European championships as a physio support. 

 

Thanks to these experiences and my 17 years of climbing I understand better climbing movements so I can help with a number of health issues associated with climbing.

 

I always put maximum emphasis on individual characteristics and differences.

About Lucas:


I live and breathe climbing. I qualified as a climbing coach (NAME) after doing a sports degree and also coaching swimming and tennis. I want to share my passion with others, and that really is climbing.
I have traveled the world for rock climbing: trad climbing on sea stacks from Scotland to Tasmania and sport climbing across Europe and Asia. I currently live most of the year in my van, but I’m also based in Rodellar when conditions are good. I love all sorts of climbing, but the more adventurous, the better!


I have an analytical mind and believe in a personalized approach to coaching. By watching you climb and observing how you move, I can identify your strengths and weaknesses and show you how to improve and develop as a climber to achieve your goals, whatever your level. Sometimes, small details can make a huge difference.

About Arturo:

Arturo is always trying to find ways of expressing himself through the movement. He started surfing at the age of 13 and kept doing it until he discovered a different and purest form of expression: climbing.

He was living and surfing in Tenerife when he started climbing in his 20s and since the beginning, he was so passionate about it that decided to move to Spain to keep pushing his limits on the vertical realm.

'The thing I love about climbing is the feeling of pushing my limits, even when my mind wants to stop I love to keep going and stay focused' Arturo says.

Nowadays Arturo spends most of his time living in his van around the walls in Sella. Looking for new projects and meeting motivated people to share climbing.

rows.name: Javier Marin Garcia
rows.body:
Javi is our main coach and guide for the Deep Water Solo Course in Mallorca, however, he can do from sport climbing, and multipitch climbing to canyoning.

 

I am Javier Marín, a certified guide since 2012, and associated with the AEGM climbing group. Climber with more than 20 years of experience, born and trained on the island of Mallorca, a paradise of quality limestone, psicobloc, and magnificent places with big walls unknown to most of the climbing community.

Since I started climbing, I have become a multipitch climber, gaining experience in this field, climbing throughout Spain, such as Ordesa, Pico Uriellu, Peña Santa, Montrebei, Montserrat, and Galayos. Also many routes in other countries such as the Media Luna peak and the Mocho in Argentine Patagonia, the Eternal Flame in the Nameless Tower in the Karakorum, Púlpito del Diablo Nevado de Guicán in Colombia, and others.

Currently live in Alicante where I am also climbing and guiding my clients, throughout the Costa Blanca. I work full time as a rock climbing guide, psicobloc, multipitch routes, trad, and big walls, mainly between Mallorca, Alicante, and the rest of Spain.

I love joining my clients' challenges and projects to be involved with them and to be able to live and enjoy the experience together. Mallorca and Alicante are incredible destinations to be able to develop as a climber and to be able to take your level and experience to a higher level

rows.name: Jose Luis Palao Lacalle
rows.body:
Jose is our coach and guide for:

About Jose:

 

My name is Jose, I’m 39 years old, and I’ve been climbing for half of my life. Over the years, I’ve had the opportunity to climb in some of the most renowned climbing areas in the world. While I’m familiar with all climbing styles, my favorite discipline is sport climbing.

 

Last year, I decided to take my passion to a professional level by earning the TD2 climbing guide certification. I also completed a 200-hour training course with one of the top coaches in Spain and an additional course focused on fear management techniques. I believe this training, combined with my university degree in Primary Education with a specialization in Physical Education, not only gives me a deep understanding of the subject matter but also the skills to teach it effectively. Additionally, having lived for five years in the United States and two in the UK, I am fully comfortable communicating in both Spanish and English.

rows.name: Pol Palau Serrano
rows.body:
Pol Palau Serrano was born in Barcelona in 1993 and is now based in the heart of the Pyrenees in Durro (Vall de Boí), Pol is a high-performance climbing guide and a National Route Setter specializing in Paraclimbing.

With a competitive pedigree that includes three Spanish Youth Championship titles and appearances on the World Cup circuit, Pol brings elite-level technical knowledge to his coaching. His personal resume speaks for itself: sport climbing up to 8b+ (8a on-sight), 8a boulders, and 7c flash. A truly versatile climber, he has also established 8a multi-pitch routes.

Currently, Pol focuses his energy on the mountains of Alta Ribagorça, opening long multi-pitch lines and developing new sectors. As a coach, his mission is to share his passion for the sport while helping climbers improve their performance and respect the ethics and environment of the crags they love.

rows.name: Kostas Grafanaki
rows.body:
The Zen Master of Greek Limestone

Based in: Leonidio, Greece

Specialties: Movement & Flow, Mental Training, Performance Coaching, Multi-pitch

Credentials: BSc Sport Science (University of Athens), Tyrolean Sport Climbing Instructor (Bergsportführer Association), Certified Yoga Teacher (Hatha)

The Story

Born on the rugged island of Crete, Kostas discovered climbing at 16 and never looked back. Unlike many who simply "climb hard," Kostas took a scientific approach to the vertical world. He moved to Athens to earn a degree in Sport Science, simultaneously climbing at a competitive level and becoming a certified coach by the Greek General Secretariat of Sports.

After years of coaching top-tier competition athletes in Athens’ climbing gyms, Kostas followed the call of the wild to Leonidio. Today, he is a cornerstone of the Greek climbing scene—not just as a coach, but as a prolific route developer and crag maintainer for the South Kynouria municipality.

The Coaching Philosophy: Performance Meets Zen

Kostas isn’t your average "pull harder" coach. His approach is deeply holistic, blending high-level sports science with the mental clarity of a certified yoga instructor (trained in Rishikesh, India).

At Rockbusters, Kostas focuses on the "Movement & Flow" aspect of climbing. He believes that peak performance happens when the physical, technical, and mental states are in perfect alignment. He specializes in helping climbers break through plateaus by identifying subtle movement inefficiencies and overcoming the psychological barriers—like the fear of falling—that hold them back from their true potential.

Why Climb with Kostas?

Whether you are transitioning from the gym to the crag or trying to unlock 8a movement, Kostas brings a calm, methodical, and deeply supportive energy to his sessions. He has a unique talent for simplifying complex technical concepts, making them accessible and actionable mid-route.

Expect to finish a week with Kostas not just as a stronger climber, but as a more mindful athlete who understands how to connect with the rock, find a state of flow, and climb with total presence.
